judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'a Loan made pursuant to Section 2.06 or Section 2.01' inverts the natural order and describes as 'made' a loan that under Section 2.06(e) arises by automatic conversion rather than by any act of making.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.06(e) (c227) deems the Term Loan into existence, and Section 2.01 (c213) says the undrawn commitment lapses at the end of the Term Loan Availability Period, so a conversion after that date is hard to reconcile with either provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed end date with an acceleration proviso; the wording itself is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Letters of Credit may be issued until 30 June 2013 with expiries up to 2014 and their disbursements automatically convert into Term Loans under Section 2.06(e), yet Sections 2.01 and 2.08(a) terminate all commitments on 30 September 2013 and Section 2.09 fixes repayment by reference to loans outstanding on that day.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'shall be set forth or in the Assignment and Assumption or Accession Agreement' contains a stray 'or' that breaks the sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It states that the Initial Lender's commitment 'is the initial Total Commitment', which matches c199 and Sections 2.02(a)-(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short additive definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 'Required Lenders' (c168) and 'Unused Commitment' (c204).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A back-reference to the Recitals.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Recital defines the Term Loan Facility as US$250,000,000 'as such amount may be increased upon any Accession Project Financing', which is the same tension the Total Commitment definition (c199) and Financial Closure (c081) raise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A straightforward two-limb definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates work done by 'Lender' (c117) and 'Term Loan Exposure' (c194) but conflicts with neither.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single fixed date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches instalment 24 of the Section 2.09 table (1 January 2020) and the Interest Period proviso that no Interest Period may end after it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The subtraction of litigation-related capital contributions is expressed in a long trailing clause that is hard to parse and turns on the vague Material Adverse Effect standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same litigation carve-out appears in c012(7) and c013(m), and 'Net Equity' (c139) subtracts Total Debt, which strips out promoter loans again, so the same amounts are adjusted in several places.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed figure with a stated maximum; the wording is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Recitals say term lenders 'shall provide' approximately US$530,000,000 and 'Financial Closure' (c081) requires Total Commitments actually to reach US$530,000,000 before Tranche B is available, so how much the Lenders were bound to commit is genuinely contestable across these provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 'without duplications' opener and three additive limbs are workable, but 'Short-Term Debt and Working Capital Bank Finance' uses a term ('Working Capital Bank Finance') that differs from the defined 'Working Capital Bank Financing'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Both c127 and c179 already exclude Working Capital Bank Financing and promoter loans, so adding Working Capital Bank Finance back here and then deducting promoter loans again risks the very double counting Section 1.03 forbids.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'all fees, costs and expenses (including fees paid for consulting and financial services)' is broad but the inclusion is illustrative and the class is anchored to the defined Transactions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its breadth is inherited from 'Transactions' (c202), which extends to 'the completion and operations of the Project', so Transaction Costs could swallow ordinary operating costs that Section 2.02(d) treats separately as Project costs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (b) — 'the completion and operations of the Project and any matters related thereto' — is essentially unbounded and sits oddly beside the tightly drawn financing steps in limb (a).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Adjusted Net Income' (c012) excludes accruals and charges 'required to be established as a result of the Transactions', and 'Transaction Costs' (c201) is defined by reference to the same term, so the breadth of limb (b) feeds straight into the financial covenants.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is a run-on that describes rather than defines — 'certain of which Unsecured Subordinated Promoter Loans are excluded from certain definitions as used herein' names neither the loans nor the definitions, and the section reference is garbled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The term is excluded from c013(l), c127(e), c138(i)(B), c179, c198 and c200 in different ways, and the payment restriction is said to sit both in the Subordination Agreement (c180) and in Section 6.07, so its treatment must be reconstructed from half a dozen other provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear subtraction formula with two identified deductions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It deducts outstanding LC Exposure, but 'LC Exposure' (c116) is itself mis-enumerated and Section 2.06(a) tests availability against the Unused Commitment 'as reduced by any Borrowings under Section 2.02(a) or (b)', which appears to deduct the same amounts twice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the providers of supplier financing to EPIL, namely, the Export-Import Bank of India and the Central Bank of India' names two banks after a general description, so whether the class is closed or merely illustrated is genuinely open (expressio unius).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Their status as Secured Parties is conditional on the upstream financing meeting the Supplier Financing definition (c185) 'including principal amount, interest rate, repayment and prepayment terms', yet c175 and c174 already treat them as Secured Parties sharing pari passu.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It ends with the same broken phrase as its siblings — 'on the same terms as the required by the Loans' — and the conditional tail makes the denominator indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the mirror image of c009 and c119 but all three key to different subsections of Section 2.11, which is not part of the reproduced instrument, so the three sharing formulas cannot be reconciled from the visible text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise 100% test with a de minimis carve-out for qualifying shares.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is used in 'Investment' (c112) although c183 states the Borrower has no Subsidiary.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A statutory cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the ERISA Event definition (c069).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short definition with an exclusion for Affiliates; the parenthetical '(other than the Borrower)' is redundant of the counterparty concept.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with c210 and with the Security Agreement proviso (c177) that subordinates Current Assets security to such a bank.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'a secured or unsecured working capital facility, including one or more financings by way of a sale, transfer or pledge of receivables' is broad and gives no size or purpose limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It drives the subordination proviso in c177, the deductions in c047, c127, c179 and c200 (the last of which calls it 'Working Capital Bank Finance'), so its perimeter matters in several inconsistent places.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard construction clause; the deeming of 'including' to mean 'without limitation' and 'will' to mean 'shall' are conventional and self-explanatory.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 'without limitation' rule works against any ejusdem generis reading of the enumerated lists in c151, c096 and c084, which is exactly the sort of interaction a court would have to work through.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long GAAP-freeze mechanism with nested provisos; the closing sentence, 'all of the financial calculations, computations and definitions hereunder shall not include any double counting', is a blanket override with no stated method of application.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Several definitions do arguably double count (c127/c179/c200 on promoter loans and working capital debt; c012 and c053 on extraordinary items), so this sentence is the provision a court would use to reconcile them and would itself have to be construed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear on availability and on the bar to re-borrowing; the only softness is that the 'maximum aggregate principal amount ... is the Total Commitment', which is a moving figure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The automatic lapse of undrawn commitments at the end of the Term Loan Availability Period (30 September 2013) cannot easily be reconciled with Section 2.06, which permits Letters of Credit outstanding into 2014 whose disbursements automatically convert into Term Loans under Section 2.06(e).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The A-2 limb refers to amounts 'not previously borrowed as contemplated by clauses (i) above', a plural/singular mismatch pointing at a single clause, and the availability is expressed as continuing 'from time to time' with no stated end.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.02(b) (c215) permits the unborrowed balance of Tranche A to be drawn only after Financial Closure, which overlaps confusingly with this clause's own availability rule, and Section 2.06(a) refers to limits on an 'Initial Lender Tranche A Commitment' not defined here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical folding the unborrowed Tranche A balance into Tranche B availability is compressed but readable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Availability turns on 'Financial Closure' (c081), which requires Total Commitments of US$530,000,000 when the Total Commitment (c199) is US$250,000,000 absent accessions — so Tranche B, and the residue of Tranche A, may never become available at all, which the Recitals' promise of a US$250,000,000 facility does not suggest.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short deferral to the Accession Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c004, c193 and Section 2.20.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the payment of the Project's costs and Transaction Costs amounts' is garbled, and 'the Project's costs' is undefined and potentially very broad given the definition of Project.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The prohibition on using proceeds to 'fund or maintain the DSRA' sits against Section 2.06(j) (c231), which routes cash collateral into the DSRA, and against the Escrow Account definition (c070), which sweeps all Borrower receipts into a single account.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proviso 'subject to Section 2.03(c)' appears to be a mis-citation — Section 2.03(c) concerns Eurodollar Rate Borrowings, whereas the constraint on non-ratable requests is the minimum-amount rule in Section 2.03(d).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Non-ratable borrowing sits awkwardly against Section 2.09 (c238), which requires repayment 'to the Facility Agent, for the ratable account of the Lenders', and against the pro rata sharing regime in Section 2.18 referred to in the table of contents.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional several-liability clause; the double statement of severalty is repetitive but clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with Section 2.08(a)'s unilateral cancellation right (c236), which allows a single Lender to withdraw its commitment entirely — a much stronger position than mere severalty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'each Borrowing shall be comprised entirely of Eurodollar Rate Borrowings' is circular — a Borrowing composed of Borrowings — and reads oddly against the definition of Eurodollar Rate Borrowing (c072), which is itself defective.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.04 (c222) says that if a Eurodollar Rate Borrowing is unavailable the Lenders 'may' fund at a different rate 'in their complete discretion', which contradicts the mandatory 'shall be comprised entirely' rule here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'in not more than fifteen (15) Borrowings' is attached to a sentence about minimum size, leaving it unclear whether the cap is per Lender, per tranche, or across the whole facility, and whether it survives an Accession Agreement's different terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because 'Borrowing' (c021) includes an LC Exposure, the fifteen-Borrowing cap could be read to count letters of credit, notwithstanding the carve-out here for LC Disbursements converted into Term Loans.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long procedural clause that is mostly mechanical, but the sentence permitting the Lenders to fund under Section 2.14 'but they shall have no obligation to do so ... in their complete discretion' converts an apparently committed facility into a discretionary one in a stated contingency.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That discretion is hard to square with Section 2.01's committed availability and Section 2.03(b)'s several funding obligations, and the required certification by 'a Responsible Officer, or other officer or director reasonably acceptable to the Facility Agent' widens the class fixed by c169.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The blanket last sentence — no liability for consequential damages 'in respect of any Borrowing requested by Borrower that is not funded by a Lender in accordance with this Agreement' — is one-sidedly drafted and its reach is unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Funds are paid into the Escrow Account, yet the Escrow Account definition (c070) says amounts there are 'to be applied in accordance with the Cash Sweep Mechanism', while this section says the Escrow Agent will make them available to the Borrower for its stated purposes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It refers to 'the applicable limitations on the Initial Lender Tranche A Commitment set forth in Section 2.02(a)', a term the Agreement never defines (the defined term is 'Initial Lender Tranche A Total Commitment'), and the reissuance proviso is a single sprawling sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It measures availability against the Unused Commitment 'as reduced by any Borrowings under Section 2.02(a) or (b)', although 'Unused Commitment' (c204) already deducts those Borrowings, and the 30 June 2013 issuance cut-off runs past the point at which Financial Closure may still be pending.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The documentary requirements are listed disjunctively as (i) to (v) and then closed by '(vi) such other documents as may be specified by the Issuing Bank from time to time', an open catch-all appended to specifics, followed by a deemed representation of the Borrower.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The deemed representation tests LC Exposure against the Unused Commitment of the reimbursing Lender, using the same double-deduction structure as Section 2.06(a) and the LC Exposure definition (c116).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-limb 'first to occur' test stated in plain terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Four years from the 29 December 2010 Agreement date is 29 December 2014, yet the 'Letter of Credit' definition (c120) permits negotiation of a letter of credit up to 30 December 2014 — a day after the last possible expiry.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The conversion trigger depends on 'the Issuing Bank ha[ving] had not less than five (5) Business Days' prior notice of such LC Disbursement', which makes no sense where it is the Issuing Bank itself that makes the disbursement, and the following sentence measures the same period from receipt of documentation instead.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Automatic conversion into a Term Loan can occur long after the Term Loan Availability Period ends and after commitments terminate under Sections 2.01 and 2.08(a), and Section 2.09 (c238) sizes repayment by reference to loans outstanding on the last day of that period.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long but carefully structured obligations-absolute clause with an express carve-back for direct damages caused by failure to exercise care; the '(iii) any other event or circumstance whatsoever' catch-all is expressly not limited by the preceding items.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its standard — liability for failure to exercise care in document examination — is inconsistent with Section 2.06(g) (c229), which says the Borrower 'will not question' the Issuing Bank's compliance decision absent gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Issuing Bank will have the final word on determining whether the documents are credit compliant or not and if, or if not, determined credit compliant the Borrower will not question its decision' is grammatically broken and one-sidedly drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It applies a gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud standard where Section 2.06(f) (c228) preserves the Issuing Bank's liability for direct damages caused by a mere failure to exercise care — two different standards for the same conduct.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short and specific interest-accrual rule with a defined rate and period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes a gap between disbursement and conversion that Section 2.06(e) (c227) creates through its confusing five-Business-Day tests, and 'Interest Payment Date' (c110) does not cover this interim interest.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger sentence stacks two alternatives ('and the Loans ... have been accelerated ... or upon the occurrence of any Event of Default ... described in clause (g) or (h)') in a way that makes it uncertain whether acceleration is required in the first limb only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cash collateral is deposited into the DSRA 'as supplemental to the Required Amount' although Section 2.02(d) (c217) forbids funding the DSRA with proceeds and Section 5.15 fixes the Required Amount; the promise to return the collateral once Events of Default are cured also assumes the acceleration can be undone.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumeration runs '(i) ... and (iii)' with no clause (ii), and a provision headed 'Interest Elections' in fact permits only one election, at the outset.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reproduces verbatim the same defect as the 'Interest Period' definition (c111), and it is in tension with 'Interest Election Request' (c108), which calls the request 'one-time' while Section 2.07(c) has the Agent notifying an Interest Period 'for each Borrowing'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and mechanical; the only oddity is that it makes the Interest Election Request part of the first Borrowing Request rather than a separate instrument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Interest Election Request' (c108) is defined as a distinct request and Section 2.04 (c222) requires the initial Interest Period to be specified in the Borrowing Request itself, so the two documents are conflated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An administrative notification duty in plain terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its second sentence contemplates the Agent advising an Interest Period 'for each Borrowing', which sits against the 'one-time' characterisation of the election in c108 and c232.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short default-rate switch conditioned on a Required Lender request and notice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defers to Section 2.13(c), which is not part of the reproduced text, and its 'notwithstanding any contrary provision hereof' opener overrides the Interest Period machinery in c111 and c232.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It lets Lenders cancel unused commitments 'for any reason, including the deterioration in the Borrower's creditworthiness due to (i)-(iii)' — an open licence dressed with enumerated examples — and it is internally inconsistent about notice, saying cancellation may occur 'upon prior written notice' and 'immediately upon such notice', while the following sentence only requires the Lenders to 'endeavor to provide prior notice' except in the creditworthiness case.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: An unfettered right to cancel is very hard to reconcile with Section 2.01's committed availability, Section 2.03(b)'s several funding obligations and Section 2.02's tranche availability on satisfaction of Articles IV conditions, and with the Recitals' statement that the Initial Lender 'is willing to provide the Facilities'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The condition — that 'the Project costs shall have been reduced below one billion ninety seven million Dollars' — uses an undefined measure of Project costs taken from the Recitals' estimate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It denies the Borrower any reduction right before Financial Closure while Section 2.08(a) (c236) gives the Lenders an unconditional cancellation right at any time, and the US$1,097,000,000 figure comes from the Recitals rather than any operative provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The obligation is to repay 'the aggregate principal amount of all Term Loans outstanding on the last day of the Term Loan Availability Period' in 24 instalments, yet the parenthetical '(or such lesser or greater principal amount as shall be outstanding on such date)' and the payment-on-'the next preceding Business Day' rule pull against the fixed percentages in the table.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Term Loans can still arise after that measuring date through the automatic conversion of LC Disbursements under Section 2.06(e), so the fixed table cannot capture the whole principal, and repayment is 'for the ratable account of the Lenders' although Section 2.03(a) allows non-ratable borrowing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short record-keeping obligation in ordinary terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It pairs with Section 2.10(b) and creates no tension elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision breaks off mid-sentence at 'the Interest Period applicable', so as reproduced it states an incomplete obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It records tranche and Interest Period information that depends on the defective Interest Period machinery in c111 and c232, but no conflict with another operative provision is visible.
